subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Turbochargers: Exhaust-Powered Boost
description: A 60-second lesson on Turbochargers: Exhaust-Powered Boost.

hook.text: Exhaust gas spins a turbine at 150,000 RPM. That turbine compresses intake air, forcing more into the engine.

buildup.text: More air means more fuel can burn per stroke. More fuel burned means more power from the same engine size.

discovery.text: A turbocharger recycles wasted exhaust energy. It boosts power without increasing engine displacement.

twist.text: Turbo lag is the delay before boost kicks in. The turbine needs exhaust flow to spin up. Patience required.

climax.text: Modern cars use tiny turbocharged engines that match the power of larger engines while using less fuel.

punchline.text: Recycle the exhaust. Boost the intake. Free power from waste.

quiz.question: What causes turbo lag in a turbocharged engine?
options: The fuel injectors can't deliver fuel fast enough to match the extra air
The turbine needs exhaust gas flow to spin up before it can compress air
The intercooler takes time to cool the compressed air before it enters
